clue.text: Lunchtime snack, possibly — and port

definitions.meaning: a filled bread snack eaten at midday, the 'possibly' allowing that it is one example
A town in Kent, one of the historic Cinque Ports on England's south coast

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the bread-and-filling snack; the other is the Kentish Cinque Port town of that name.

clue.text: Fellow in a university town initially inspiring admiration

indicators.note: the fellow's name sits inside the run built from the other pieces
initially means only the opening letter of town is used

parts.note: Gus is a man's name, so a fellow

explanation.surface: An academic in a college town is held in high regard from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means majestic and venerable, something that inspires reverence or admiration.

clue.text: Vestment used by cathedral bigwig

indicators.note: the letters needed are employed by the run of words cathedral bigwig, spanning its word break

explanation.surface: A priestly robe worn by a senior churchman at the cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: An alb is a long white linen robe worn by clergy at the Eucharist, a liturgical vestment.

clue.text: Free film making a comeback in spring?

indicators.note: the turned film word goes inside the word for spring

parts.note: to spring from a source is to emanate from it

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word for film is read backwards

parts.note: a pic is a film, short for picture

explanation.surface: A free movie is returning to screens in the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season, but here it is a verb meaning to issue from; 'making a comeback' is the reversal signal on the film word.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate is to free someone from legal or social restraint, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Force to find permanent way across the pond?

definitions.meaning: to push or coerce someone into acting hastily
the permanent way is the track bed of a railway, and across the pond means in American usage

explanation.definitionFit: To railroad someone is to force them; Americans call a railway a railroad.

clue.text: See about taking course and getting on

indicators.note: about tells us to turn the word for see round

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a dish is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: Have a look around, take a course, and grow older.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for ageing, and oldish describes someone somewhat advanced in years.

clue.text: Wave dislodging second fish

indicators.note: dislodging means knocking out, so the letter for second is removed

parts.note: to shake something is to wave it about

explanation.surface: A wave knocks a second fish off the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The hake is an edible sea fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Happened to be at sea, celebrating with drink

parts.note: was is the past of be, so happened to be
sailing means travelling on the sea

explanation.surface: Someone who happened to be on a ship was toasting with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassailing is the old custom of drinking healths and carousing at festivals.

clue.text: Granny gets ring back — in practically no time

parts.note: nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
O is ring-shaped
to second someone is to back or support them

explanation.surface: A grandmother gets her ring returned almost at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal but is SECOND, meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanosecond is a billionth of a second, so figuratively almost no time at all.

clue.text: Hot water in the officers' place

definitions.meaning: being in hot water means being in trouble or a muddle
the officers' ... is where military officers eat together

explanation.definitionFit: Hot water is trouble or a muddle; a military dining room is called a mess.

clue.text: Lied about right back being sturdy?

indicators.note: the word for Lied goes round the turned letters

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song

indicators.note: back tells us to read the abbreviation for right backwards

explanation.surface: Someone told untruths regarding having a sound back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lied' reads as the past of lie but is the German noun for a song; 'back' turns RT to TR.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong and sturdy are synonyms, both meaning robust and solidly built.

clue.text: Condescending supporter of Charles I

definitions.meaning: a Royalist in the English Civil War was known as a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is offhand or haughty; the Royalist backers of Charles I were Cavaliers.

clue.text: Dejected priests still regularly misinterpreted

indicators.note: misinterpreted suggests the letters are read wrongly and so rearranged
regularly means every other letter of still is taken

explanation.surface: Downcast clergy are still being misunderstood from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes SIL from 'still'; that and PRIESTS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritless means lacking vigour or courage, a synonym of dejected and downcast.

clue.text: Poisonous type dropping second article in without delay

indicators.note: dropping second means the later of the two article letters is let fall

parts.note: ASAP is short for as soon as possible
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A venomous person drops the second item in at once.
explanation.definitionFit: An asp is a small venomous snake, so a poisonous type of creature.

clue.text: Fool in school becoming informer

indicators.note: the fool goes inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: nit is short for nitwit, a fool

explanation.surface: The class clown turns tell-tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A snitch is slang for someone who tells tales, an informer.

clue.text: Shame I'm suffering! British woman in India once?

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shame from a colonial-era British lady in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British' looks like part of the definition, but it gives the final B.
explanation.definitionFit: Memsahib was the term used in colonial India for a European married woman.

clue.text: Marine animal hunting mostly around western fringe of Uist

indicators.note: the shortened word for hunting goes round the letter taken from Uist
mostly means the last letter is cut

parts.note: searching is hunting for something

indicators.note: the western fringe of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Hunting for a sea creature along the west coast of a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Uist is an island in the Outer Hebrides off Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a spiny marine echinoderm, a sea-dwelling animal.

clue.text: Pinch about one pound going over old club

indicators.note: the word for pinch goes round the turned letters

parts.note: to nick something is to pinch or steal it

indicators.note: going over means turning over, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
LB is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: Stealing an old golf club worth about a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns ILB to BLI, which sits inside NICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick was an old golf club, roughly equivalent to a modern nine iron.

clue.text: Shallow boat in west, a woman's form of transport

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A lady in the west of the country gets about by flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or a broad shallow barge used on rivers.

clue.text: Endless opportunity to secure horse for coach once

indicators.note: to secure means to hold, so the shortened word grips the horse
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: Unending opportunity to hitch a horse to an old coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc was an early open motor coach used for outings, now obsolete.

clue.text: Fresh air unknown over a southern state

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Z is a mathematical unknown
on means over, as in on top of

explanation.surface: Fresh air and the unknown over a state in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is a US state in the Southwest, on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Sporting triumph that's attractive, bringing in foreign cash

indicators.note: the word for attractive brings the cash inside it

parts.note: glam is short for glamorous
rands are South African currency

explanation.surface: A glamorous sports victory that pulls in money from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand slam is winning every major event in a sport in a season, a supreme triumph.

clue.text: Family member changing wide-brimmed hat in the centre

indicators.note: changing means one letter is replaced by another
the letter replaced is the middle one of the hat

parts.note: a Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat

explanation.surface: A relative swaps his broad-brimmed hat halfway through.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue only says the centre letter changes; the new P comes from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepson is the son of one's spouse from a former relationship, a family member.

clue.text: Green pass old soldiers captured in film

indicators.note: the pieces are captured inside the film title

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film
a col is a mountain pass
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Inexperienced old troops are caught on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like an adjective meaning naive, but defines an environmentalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A Green is an environmental campaigner, and an ecologist is a common term for one.

clue.text: Healthy son entering function, a native of Colombo, perhaps

indicators.note: the healthy son goes into the trig function

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
hale means healthy

explanation.surface: A fit boy goes to an event and meets a person from Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: Colombo is Sri Lanka's capital, not Colombia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinhalese are the majority people of Sri Lanka, whose largest city is Colombo.

clue.text: Organised a stop, grub being available here?

definitions.text: Organised a stop, grub being available here?

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arranging a break where food is served.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub that serves high-quality food, so grub is on offer there.

clue.text: Skilled workman taking sides? Not the first

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for taking sides is dropped

parts.note: partisan means taking sides, biased

explanation.surface: A tradesman gets involved in a dispute, but not straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker or craftsman.

clue.text: Language no good in priest's hole initially

indicators.note: the letters for no good go inside the rest

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

indicators.note: only the first letter of hole is used

explanation.surface: A language no good in a priest hole at first.
explanation.walkthrough: A priest's hole was a hiding place for Catholic priests in English houses; here 'priest's' is ELI'S.
explanation.definitionFit: English is the language of England and much of the world.

clue.text: Inscription not displayed until someone's bought it?

definitions.text: Inscription not displayed until someone's bought it?

parts.words: Inscription not displayed until someone's bought it?
parts.note: bought it is slang for died; the inscription meant appears on a tombstone after death

explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the tribute carved on a gravestone, put up after a death.

clue.text: Syrupy drink made by accountant's little sibling

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
sis is a short form of sister

explanation.surface: A drink prepared by the accountant's younger sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur, sweet and syrupy.
